description: This cluster describes fundamental patterns for AI agents to operate autonomously and intelligently. It encompasses mechanisms for self-correction, continuous learning, adaptation to dynamic environments, structured planning, goal management, and advanced reasoning to achieve complex objectives.

This cluster encompasses patterns that extend Large Language Models' (LLMs) capabilities beyond text generation by enabling them to interact with external systems, perform actions, and access real-time information. This is achieved through the integration and utilization of various tools (e.g., APIs, functions, databases, web search), either via dynamic LLM orchestration or predefined execution sequences.

This cluster covers patterns for designing AI systems, from single autonomous agents to complex multi-agent collaborations. It includes strategies for task decomposition, dynamic delegation, collaborative refinement, and orchestration of specialized agents to solve complex problems and enhance output quality.

This cluster focuses on enhancing Large Language Models (LLMs) by integrating external knowledge retrieval. It addresses LLM limitations like hallucinations, outdated information, and lack of domain-specific knowledge by fetching relevant data from external sources and providing it as context for generation. This improves factual accuracy, explainability, and contextual relevance, often involving the selection of an appropriate generative model.

This cluster encompasses sophisticated methods for training AI agents, primarily in Reinforcement Learning. Patterns address challenges like achieving superhuman performance, accelerating complex skill acquisition, safely training for physical tasks, improving generalization across environments, and bridging the simulation-to-reality gap.

This cluster encompasses diverse advanced machine learning patterns focused on enhancing model performance, robustness, and efficiency. It includes strategies for sophisticated data preparation and representation (e.g., feature engineering, embeddings, multimodal inputs, data augmentation, rebalancing), leveraging existing knowledge (transfer learning, knowledge distillation, self-supervised learning), combining multiple models (ensembles), and optimizing the learning process (hyperparameter tuning, multitask learning, anomaly detection strategies).

This cluster focuses on patterns that enhance AI system safety, reliability, and trustworthiness. It includes strategies to mitigate risks like errors, hallucinations, and harmful outputs through guardrails, redundancy, and robust error handling. A core theme is integrating human oversight (Human-in-the-Loop) for critical decisions, validation, and graceful degradation, ensuring ethical and controlled AI operation.

This cluster describes patterns for using Large Language Models (LLMs) as high-level planners for embodied agents and robotics. Key themes include grounding LLM plans in the physical environment, adapting to dynamic conditions via feedback loops and environmental context, and improving planning efficiency through few-shot learning and prompt engineering.
sub_patterns: External Affordance Function for LLM Planning

description: This cluster describes patterns for using Large Language Models (LLMs) as agent policies in interactive environments. It emphasizes finetuning LLMs with Reinforcement Learning (RL) for 'functional grounding,' enabling them to understand and act upon environmental dynamics. Patterns cover action probability calculation, architectural integrations (value heads, prompt structuring), scaling, and generalization capabilities.
sub_patterns: Online Reinforcement Learning for LLM Finetuning
Value Head Integration for LLM-based RL
Contextual Prompt Structuring for RL Agents

description: This cluster covers advanced RAG patterns enhancing intelligence, adaptability, and accuracy. It features agentic orchestration for dynamic routing and multi-step reasoning, adaptive retrieval strategies, iterative refinement and self-correction, and sophisticated prompt engineering. It also includes methods for leveraging diverse data sources, including graph knowledge, and optimizing performance through targeted retrieval and generation control.
sub_patterns: Graph-Enhanced Agent for Retrieval Augmented Generation (GEAR)

description: This cluster focuses on advanced retrieval methods that leverage various graph structures (knowledge graphs, hierarchical documents, community graphs) to provide richer, more structured, or contextually relevant information to LLMs. Patterns combine vector search with graph traversal or querying to move beyond simple text chunks, incorporating relationships, hierarchies, and entity-specific details for more precise or comprehensive context.

Focuses on retrieving, processing, and preparing text for AI/LLMs. Includes lexical, semantic, and hybrid search, document chunking, metadata use, and advanced techniques to enhance retrieval accuracy and context.

This cluster encompasses techniques designed to enhance the relevance and precision of information retrieval. It includes patterns for transforming user queries into more effective search inputs and re-ranking initial search results to prioritize the most relevant documents, often leveraging advanced language models.

This cluster describes the process of adapting pre-trained generative models, particularly LLMs, to specific domains, tasks, or desired styles. It involves continuing the model's training on smaller, specialized datasets to enhance performance, accuracy, and domain-specific knowledge beyond what general models or RAG can achieve.

This cluster describes core patterns for designing intelligent AI agents, covering how they generate and refine plans (single-shot, incremental, multi-path), incorporate feedback (self, cross, human reflection), understand and clarify user goals (passive, proactive), and integrate external tools or agents (adapters, registries). These patterns enhance agent reasoning, adaptability, and interaction.

This cluster encompasses diverse strategies for interacting with LLMs, ranging from basic direct prompts and system instructions to advanced multi-step reasoning (e.g., Chain-of-Thought, Least-to-Most), task decomposition, and agentic patterns (e.g., ReAct) that interleave reasoning with actions and tool use. These patterns aim to improve LLM accuracy, control, transparency, and ability to solve complex, interactive problems.
sub_patterns: Prompt Engineering for Grounding and Factuality

description: This cluster encompasses patterns for designing and managing multi-agent AI systems. It focuses on how multiple specialized agents collaborate, communicate, and coordinate to solve complex problems through task decomposition, role assignment, communication protocols, and structured workflows.

This cluster focuses on systematic processes and tooling for assessing the performance, reliability, and quality of AI models, especially LLMs and agents. It addresses non-determinism by defining metrics, creating test scenarios, and integrating evaluation into development pipelines to ensure intended behavior and continuous improvement.

This cluster encompasses patterns for integrating Responsible AI (RAI) principles across the entire AI system lifecycle. It covers requirements, design, development, testing, deployment, and continuous monitoring, focusing on explainability, fairness, accountability, and risk management.
sub_patterns: Verifiable claim for AI system artifacts
Extensible adaptive and dynamic RAI risk assessment

description: This cluster encompasses AI patterns designed to enable collaborative model training and efficient inference while prioritizing data privacy, security, and distributed execution. Key themes include keeping sensitive data local, secure aggregation of model updates, training on encrypted data, and optimizing predictions across edge and cloud environments.
sub_patterns: Data Flows Up Model Flows Down

description: This cluster encompasses patterns for managing the lifecycle, movement, communication, and coordination of mobile agents in distributed environments. It addresses challenges like agent discovery, navigation, task delegation, asynchronous interaction, and secure data handling during travel.

This cluster covers patterns for robust ML system deployment and continuous monitoring (e.g., canary releases, ongoing evaluation), alongside context-driven automation of ML workflow design. It includes data preparation, algorithm selection, and metric evaluation based on user, data, and model characteristics, linking business goals to ML insights.
sub_patterns: Algorithm Categorization and Selection for Analytics Goals

description: This cluster focuses on classifying diverse inputs (queries, tasks) and dynamically routing them to specialized prompts, models, agents, or workflows to optimize processing, efficiency, and response quality.

This cluster focuses on enhancing AI agent capabilities and efficiency. It addresses challenges like managing LLM context windows and memory for long-term coherence, personalization, and complex tasks, alongside optimizing resource usage, cost, and latency through strategic model selection and task decomposition in multi-stage AI systems.
Ensuring the health, performance, reliability, and safety of AI systems and agents in production through continuous monitoring, evaluation, and proactive issue identification.

This cluster encompasses patterns for designing and managing robust, scalable, and efficient machine learning systems. It covers strategies for distributed training, decoupling ML pipelines and workloads, ensuring data consistency between training and serving, and providing resilience for long-running training jobs.

Decouple Training Pipeline from Production Pipeline

description: This cluster focuses on architectural and development best practices for building maintainable, adaptable, and robust ML systems. description: This cluster focuses on architectural patterns for deploying, serving, and managing machine learning models and data in production environments. It covers scalable inference, data processing architectures, workflow orchestration, and microservice-based modularity.

This cluster addresses the inherent instability and unreliability of ML models, especially in critical systems. Patterns here advocate for encapsulating ML models and validating their outputs using deterministic, rule-based safeguards and quality checks to enhance robustness, safety, and trustworthiness against adversarial attacks, noise, and data drift.

description: This cluster focuses on enhancing LLM trustworthiness and transparency by providing direct citations or references to source materials, enabling users to verify factual claims and understand information provenance.

This cluster focuses on patterns where LLMs iteratively evaluate, critique, and refine their own or other LLM outputs to enhance quality, accuracy, and reliability. It leverages automated feedback loops, often incorporating external tools for verification, to achieve self-correction and improve generated content.

This cluster focuses on patterns that enable Large Language Models (LLMs) to translate natural language user questions into structured Cypher queries for retrieving data from knowledge graphs. The patterns vary in their approach, from using predefined templates for known query types to dynamically generating queries from reusable snippets or directly from the database schema for maximum flexibility.
